skill.name: jsonlogic
skill.description: Create, explain, debug, and test JsonLogic business rules. Includes Ruby execution, structural validation, operator references, and an interactive playground template.
skill.summary: Translate business conditions into JsonLogic rules and verify their behavior with representative tests.
skill.author: valeryia-piatrova

security_audit.summary: Of 372 static findings, 370 are false positives and two confirm automatic installation of an unpinned Ruby dependency. Additional findings concern artifact publication without consent and unsafe JSON embedding in HTML. No evidence found of credential theft or instructions to override this audit.

remediation.issue: The Ruby runner automatically installs an unpinned dependency.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before installation. Pin reviewed dependency versions in a lockfile and install them separately in an isolated environment.

remediation.issue: The playground workflow publishes rules and sample data without explicit consent.
remediation.suggestion: Make publication optional and ask permission before uploading data. Offer a local preview and use redacted or synthetic samples by default.

remediation.issue: Serialized rule and data values are inserted into an HTML script block without HTML-safe escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Escape every less-than character as a Unicode escape before embedding JSON. Apply this to all placeholders and test script-closing input strings.

content.user_title: Build and Test JsonLogic Business Rules
content.value_statement: Business conditions can produce unexpected results when field names, missing values, or library behavior differ. This skill builds JsonLogic rules and guides targeted verification.
actual_capabilities: Translate business requirements into JsonLogic expressions using schema or sample field names.
Explain operators, expected inputs, returned values, and edge cases in existing rules.
Check rule structure with the bundled Ruby validator without executing the rule.
Execute rules with the Ruby runner when json-logic-rb is available.
Build editable playground artifacts with live results from the bundled JavaScript interpreter.
Use bundled operator tests and library references to investigate compatibility differences.
limitations: The structural validator does not prove business correctness or support in a selected library.
The playground implements a subset and approximation, not guaranteed parity with every target library.
Execution requires a compatible runtime and dependencies; the Ruby runner attempts automatic gem installation when its dependency is absent.
Artifact publication requires client tooling and may upload data; the current template also needs safer HTML embedding.

use_cases.title: Encode Eligibility Conditions
use_cases.description: Turn product requirements into explicit rules with documented inputs, outputs, and missing-field behavior.
use_cases.target_user: Product analysts working with engineering teams

use_cases.title: Debug Application Rules
use_cases.description: Reproduce unexpected results, identify coercion or operator issues, and verify corrections against representative data.

use_cases.title: Compare Rule Implementations
use_cases.description: Test identical inputs across frontend and backend libraries to identify unsupported operators and behavior differences.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this JsonLogic rule: [rule]. Describe each operator, required fields, returned values, and missing-field behavior. Do not publish an artifact.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Business Rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a JsonLogic rule for [condition] using [schema or synthetic sample]. Explain assumptions and expected outcomes. Keep all data local.

prompt_templates.title: Debug and Verify
prompt_templates.prompt: Debug [rule] with [synthetic input] in [library and version]. Expected: [result]. Add boundary tests and request permission before installing dependencies or publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: reproduce and correct unexpected behavior

prompt_templates.title: Compare Library Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [rule] in [library A] and [library B] using identical synthetic cases. Cover missing values, coercion, and empty arrays. Separate observed from unverified results.

output_examples.input: Create a discount eligibility rule for loyalty members who spent more than 100.
output_examples.output: Eligibility requires loyalty membership and spending above 100. Spending exactly 100 does not qualify. Define missing-field handling before testing.

output_examples.input: Explain why an order rule flags an item priced at 620 when the threshold is 500.
output_examples.output: The rule checks each item and succeeds when any price exceeds 500. An item priced at 620 qualifies. An empty item list returns false.

output_examples.input: Does passing structural validation prove that my rule works in both JavaScript and Ruby?
output_examples.output: No. Structural validation checks rule shape only. Execute identical boundary, missing-field, and type cases in both libraries before claiming matching behavior.

best_practices: Provide a schema or synthetic sample and specify the target library and version.
Test normal cases, exact boundaries, missing fields, unexpected types, and empty arrays in the actual evaluator.
Use redacted inputs and explicitly approve dependency installation or artifact publication before either occurs.
anti_patterns: Treating structural validation or a playground result as proof of production correctness.
Assuming all libraries support the same extensions, truthiness rules, and type coercion.
Providing secrets or production records for automatic artifact publication.

faq.question: What is JsonLogic?
faq.answer: JsonLogic represents conditional rules as JSON objects. Libraries evaluate those rules against supplied data.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Execution and artifact support depend on the client and available tools.

faq.question: Which evaluator is used by default?
faq.answer: The default runner uses Ruby and json-logic-rb. You can request a specific library; other runtimes and dependencies must be available separately.

faq.question: Can it validate rules without executing them?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled Ruby validator checks structure using standard libraries. It does not establish business correctness or target-library compatibility.

faq.question: Does the playground match every library?
faq.answer: No. It uses a bundled JavaScript subset with a Ruby truthiness mode. Verify important results in your selected implementation.

faq.question: Does using the skill require network access?
faq.answer: Reading references and structural validation can work offline. Missing gem installation, hosted artifact publication, and external playground fonts require network access.
